description: Changes one charge where it sits — its amount, its day, its paid mark, the day the money moved, its note. The commitment is named by id or the exact name as the memory holds it — a miss answers with the real names, and `date` is the day the row sits on. `set.date` moves it: alone, the row keeps its amount as the owner's fact; with `and_later` every unpaid planned row after it follows a cycle apart and keeps its amount, and paid or hand-priced rows stay. `set.amount` with `and_later` reprices the unpaid planned rows after it too, and the commitment's price with them. A day that already holds a charge is refused, and so is a move past the cancelling date. Null clears paid_on or the note. mark_paid is the one-field way to mark. Writes are schema-validated and provenance-stamped, and land in the app's Proposals screen where the owner keeps or undoes the whole batch. Card numbers, CVVs and credentials are refused by the validator, which names the row. `source` ("documents/hdfc-2026.pdf", "gmail:18c2…") records where a row came from in the diff.

date.description: The day the charge sits on.

guide_key.description: The guide_key read_guide returned with the prompt or chapter this write follows.

amount.description: A number, zero or more, up to 1,000,000,000,000,000.

and_later.description: Reach the unpaid planned rows after it: they follow a move a cycle apart, keeping their amounts, and take a new amount with the commitment's price.

date.description: The day to move it to. A day that already holds a charge is refused.

note.description: A word about this one charge. Null clears.

paid_on.description: The day the money moved, when it was not the due date. Null clears.

name: update_charge
title: Change a charge
